headline: Jamaat MP’s son-in-law arrested over attack on building housing Salman Muqtadir’s studio
summary: Mizanur Rahman, 59, son-in-law of Jamaat-e-Islami lawmaker Md Abdul Gafur, was apprehended by DB Gulshan Division in connection with the September 27 vandalism case.
details: Police on Monday arrested Mizanur Rahman, 59, son-in-law of Jamaat-e-Islami lawmaker of Kushtia-2 Md Abdul Gafur. He was apprehended in connection with a case filed over an attack on New Gini Properties in Dhaka's ECB Chattar area.

A team from DB Gulshan Division picked him up from his house in Dhaka’s Paschim Matikata around 5:00 PM. Mizanur is listed as accused number 9 in the case, which was filed with Cantonment Police Station on September 27.
Content creator Salman Muqtadir rented a floor of the attacked building from New Gini Properties for his studio. Police confirmed that his studio was also vandalized during the incident.
caption:
A Jamaat-e-Islami lawmaker's son-in-law has been arrested in connection with the attack on a building in Dhaka.

Police on Monday arrested Mizanur Rahman, 59, son-in-law of Jamaat-e-Islami lawmaker of Kushtia-2 Md Abdul Gafur. He was apprehended in connection with a case filed over an attack on New Gini Properties in Dhaka's ECB Chattar area.

A team from DB Gulshan Division picked him up from his house in Dhaka’s Paschim Matikata around 5:00 PM. Mizanur is listed as accused number 9 in the case, which was filed with Cantonment Police Station on September 27.

Content creator Salman Muqtadir rented a floor of the attacked building from New Gini Properties for his studio. Police confirmed that his studio was also vandalized during the incident.

headline_marked: Iran's leader says [[US will be forced to leave Middle East]] after 'painful blows'
headline: Iran's leader says US will be forced to leave Middle East after 'painful blows'
summary: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei claims the US will soon exit the region, while indirect talks mediated by Qatar attempt to resolve the conflict.
details: Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei stated that the United States will be forced to leave the Middle East after suffering "painful blows." He claimed that enemies no longer venture beyond the Arabian Sea due to the actions of "valiant fighters."

The remarks come amid efforts to revive talks to end the fighting. While US President Donald Trump expressed expectation for negotiations, Iran's delegation to the UN General Assembly reported no plans for such talks in New York.

Iran has presented seven conditions for ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for 20% of the world's oil and gas. These include a seven-day ceasefire across the Middle East, including Lebanon.
Further Iranian demands include the unfreezing of foreign assets, the lifting of oil sector sanctions, and an end to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

Tensions remain high as the US recently imposed restrictions on Iran's entire aviation industry, leading to the cancellation of international flights. Iran has lodged a complaint with the UN over these sanctions.

Separately, Iran has denied involvement in a suspected bomb plot at a UK airbase used by the US. UK counter-terror police arrested five London-based Britons in connection with the security scare at RAF Fairford.
caption:
Iran's Supreme Leader claims the US will be forced out of the Middle East. Will indirect talks mediated by Qatar break the deadlock?

Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei stated that the United States will be forced to leave the Middle East after suffering "painful blows." He claimed that enemies no longer venture beyond the Arabian Sea due to the actions of "valiant fighters."

The remarks come amid efforts to revive talks to end the fighting. While US President Donald Trump expressed expectation for negotiations, Iran's delegation to the UN General Assembly reported no plans for such talks in New York.

Iran has presented seven conditions for ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for 20% of the world's oil and gas. These include a seven-day ceasefire across the Middle East, including Lebanon.

Further Iranian demands include the unfreezing of foreign assets, the lifting of oil sector sanctions, and an end to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

Tensions remain high as the US recently imposed restrictions on Iran's entire aviation industry, leading to the cancellation of international flights. Iran has lodged a complaint with the UN over these sanctions.

Separately, Iran has denied involvement in a suspected bomb plot at a UK airbase used by the US. UK counter-terror police arrested five London-based Britons in connection with the security scare at RAF Fairford.
